farraa:88-88.t: His saying: ﴿وَجِئْنَا بِبِضَاعَةٍ مُّزْجَاةٍ﴾ ("and we have come with goods of little value"). They mentioned that they came to Egypt with goods, which they sold for dirhams that would not pass in buying food except at a rate other than that of good coins; so they asked Yūsuf to take them from them without giving them less. That is His saying: ﴿ فَأَوْفِ لَنَا ٱلْكَيْلَ وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَآ﴾ ("so give us full measure and be charitable to us") — with the difference between the two rates.

farraa:93-94.t:
His saying: ﴿يَأْتِ بَصِيراً﴾ means: he will become seeing again.
His saying: ﴿لَوْلاَ أَن تُفَنِّدُونِ﴾ He is saying: [were it not that] you call me a liar, call me incapable and call me weak [of mind].

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿سَوْفَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّيۤ﴾ ("I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord"). He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us (from) Sharīk, from al-Suddī, concerning this verse: he put them off until the pre-dawn hour (saḥar). (Abū Zakariyyā said: and Ḥibbān added for us, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: he put them off until the pre-dawn hour) of the night before Friday.

farraa:105-105.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن آيَةٍ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾ ("and how many a sign in the heavens and the earth"). The signs of the heavens are the sun, the moon and the stars; and the signs of the earth are the mountains, the rivers and the like.

farraa:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ بِٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ وَهُمْ مُّشْرِكُونَ﴾ ("and most of them do not believe in Allah except while associating others with Him"). He is saying: if you ask them, "Who created you?" they say, "Allah"; or "Who provides for you?" they say, "Allah"; yet they associate others with Him and worship idols. That is His saying: ﴿وَمَا يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ بِٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ وَهُمْ مُّشْرِكُونَ﴾.

farraa:108-108.t: His saying: ﴿أَنَاْ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِي﴾ He is saying: I and whoever follows me — he too calls with clear insight, just as I call.

farraa:109-109.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَدَارُ ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ ("and the abode of the Hereafter"). "Abode" (al-dār) is put in iḍāfa (genitive construct) to "the Hereafter" (al-ākhira) although it is itself the Hereafter; the Arabs sometimes annex a thing to itself when its wording differs, as in His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ اليَقِينِ﴾ ("this is indeed the truth of certainty"), where the truth is the certainty. Similar to it is: "I came to you on the night (bāriḥa) of the first", "the year of the first", "the night of the first", and "the day of Thursday". All the days are annexed to themselves because their wording differs; likewise "the month of Rabīʿ". And the Arabs say in their speech — one of them recited to me:

أَتمدح فَقْعَساً وتذمّ عَبْساً * أَلا للهِ أُمُّك من هَجِين
ولو أقوت عَليك ديار عَبْس * عرفتَ الذُلَّ عِرفان اليقين
(Do you praise Faqʿas and blame ʿAbs? — By God, what a base-born one you are! / Had the dwellings of ʿAbs become empty for you, you would have known humiliation with the knowledge of certainty.)

Its meaning is only: a knowing and a certainty.

farraa:110-110.t:
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا ٱسْتَيْأَسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُواْ﴾ — light (without doubling). The people of Medina read it with doubling (kudhdhibū), and Ibn ʿAbbās read it light and explained it: until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing, and their people thought that the messengers had been lied to, Our help came to them. And (كُذِّبُوا) with doubling is reported from ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd].

His saying: ﴿فَنَجى مَنْ نَشَاء﴾ — the reading is with two nūns, while the written text (the muṣḥaf) has come with one nūn. ʿĀṣim read (فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَّشَآءُ), making it a single nūn, as though he disliked adding a nūn; (مَنْ) is then in the position of the nominative. As for those who read it with two nūns, the second nūn is concealed (ikhfāʾ) and does not issue from a place other than that of the first; so when it was concealed it was dropped [in writing] — do you not see that you do not say fanunjī with the nūn pronounced distinctly? So when the second was concealed it was dropped and the first nūn sufficed for it, just as one letter of two suffices, so that it is assimilated and the two are written as one.

farraa:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿مَا كَانَ حَدِيثاً يُفْتَرَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ﴾ — [تصديق is] accusative (manṣūb), meaning: but it was a confirmation of what came before it of the Scriptures: the Torah and the Gospel. Had you made التصديق nominative it would be correct, as you say: "This was not standing but sitting (qāʿidan)" and "sitting (qāʿidun)". Likewise His saying: ﴿مَا كانَ مُحمَّدٌ أَبَا أَحَدٍ مِنْ رِجَالِكُم وَلَكِنْ رَسُولَ اللهِ﴾ ("Muḥammad is not the father of any of your men, but the Messenger of Allah") and ﴿رَسُولُ اللهِ﴾ [in the nominative]: whoever reads it in the nominative does not imply kāna; he means: but he is the Messenger of Allah.

farraa:3-3.t: The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ﴾. (هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ) is accusative (manṣūb) by the verb falling upon it, as though you said: "by Our revealing to you this Qurʾān." Had you put (هذا) and (القرآنَ) in the genitive (khafḍ), it would be correct: you make (هذا) a repetition of (ما), as you say: «مررت بما عندك متاعِك» ("I passed by what you have — your goods"), making «المتاع» refer back to (مَا). Like it in al-Naḥl: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ ألْسِنَتِكُمْ الكَذِبَ﴾, and (الكَذِبِ) [in the genitive] on that basis.

farraa:4-5.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أبَتِ﴾: do not pause on it with hāʾ while you give it kasra in continuous recitation, because that kasra indicates annexation to the speaker. Were a reader to read (يا أَبَتُ), it would be permissible (and pausing on the hāʾ would be permissible), but no one we know has read it so. Were it said (يا أبَتَ), pausing on it (with hāʾ) would be permissible in one respect and not permissible in another. As for the permissibility of pausing on the hāʾ, it is that you make the fatḥa in it a fatḥa of the vocative and do not intend to join it to the alif of lamentation (alif al-nudba); so it is like the saying of the poet:
* كِلِينِى لِهَمٍّ يا أُميمةَ ناصبِ *
(Leave me, O Umayma, to a wearying care.)
As for the respect in which pausing on the hāʾ is not permissible, it is that you intend «يا أبتاه», then drop the hāʾ and the alif; for in intention it is joined to the alif just as, in the genitive, it is joined to the speaker's yāʾ.
As for His saying: ﴿إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً﴾: the Arabs make the numbers from eleven to nineteen accusative [i.e. fixed with fatḥa] in their genitive and nominative. That is because they made two known nouns into one; they did not annex the first to the second, which would take it out of the meaning of number, nor did they put its last part in the nominative, which would make it like «بعلبكّ» when they put its end in the nominative. They allowed themselves to annex «بعل» to «بَكّ» because in this one part is not recognised as separable from the other; but the five is separable from the ten and the ten from the five, so they gave them a single i'rab, because their meaning originally is "ten and five." When the two were diverted from their proper way, they were given one inflection in declension, as their inflection had been one before they were diverted.
As for the accusative of «كوكب», it came out as a specification (mufassir) of the kind for every number, so that what you are speaking of may be known. In speech it is like your saying: «عندى كذا وكذا درهماً» ("I have so-and-so many dirhams"): «الدرهم» came out as a specification of «كذا وكذا», because it can apply to anything. If you bring the alif and lām into «أحد عشر», you bring them in at its beginning and say: «ما فعلت الخمسةَ عَشَرَ؟» ("what did the fifteen do?"). It is also permissible to say «ما فعلت الخمسةَ العشرَ», bringing in the alif and lām twice, because they imagine the one as separable from the other in a certain state. But if you say «الخمسة العشرِ» [annexing], it is not permissible, because the first is other than the second; do you not see that in their saying «ما فعلت الخمسةُ الأثوابِ» — for whoever permits it — you find that the five are the garments, but you do not find the ten to be the five? That is why its annexation with alif and lām is not sound. If you wish, you may also bring the alif and lām into the dirham that comes out as a specification, and say: «ما فعلت الخمسة العشر الدرهم؟».
When you annex «الخمسة العشر» to yourself, you put «الخمسة» in the nominative and say: «ما فعلت الخمسةُ عشرِى؟», «ورأيت خمسةَ عَشْرِى» («ومررت بخمسة عشرى»). «الخمسة» received inflection only because you annexed «العشر»; since «العشر» was annexed to your yāʾ, it was not sound for «الخمسة» to be annexed to it with «عشر» between them, so it was annexed to «عشر» in order to become a noun, just as what follows it became a noun by annexation. I heard it from Abū Faqʿas al-Asadī and Abū al-Haytham al-ʿUqaylī: «ما فعلت خمسةُ عشرِك؟» ("what did your fifteen do?"). For that reason it is not sound for the specifying noun to accompany them, because their two inflections have differed. «[Note: MS B: «اختلف».]» The dirham and the star come out as a specification for both of them together, just as the dirham comes out of «عشرين» as a specification of all of it. When you annex «العشرين», it enters among nouns and specification no longer applies to it. So it is an error to say: «ما فعلت عِشروك درهماً» or «خمسةُ عشرِك درهماً». Like it is that you say: «مررت بضارب زيداً» ("I passed by one beating Zayd"); but if you annex «الضارب» to other than Zayd, it can never fall upon Zayd. «[Translator's note: the source marks the variant with «ب: اختلف», apparently a manuscript variant inserted in the text.]»
Were you to intend, in «خمسة عشر», to annex the five to the ten in poetry, it would be permissible, and you would say: «ما رأيت خمسةَ عشرٍ قطُّ خيراً منها» ("I never saw a fifteen better than it"), because you intended nouns and did not intend number. The specifying noun may not come in here, just as it was not allowed in annexation. al-ʿUklī Abū Tharwān recited to me:
كُلِّف من عَنَائه وشِقْوتهْ * بنت ثمانى عَشرةٍ من حِجتَّهْ
(Out of his toil and his misery he fell in love with a girl of eighteen years of age.)
Some readers make the ʿayn of «عشر» quiescent in all this type, except «اثنا عشر». That is because they found the many vowels heavy; and they found the alif in (اثنا) and the yāʾ in (اثنى) quiescent, so they disliked making the ʿayn quiescent with a quiescent letter beside it. (Making the ʿayn quiescent is not permissible in the feminine of the number, because the shīn of «عشرة» is quiescent, and it is not right to make both the ʿayn and the shīn quiescent.)
As for His saying ﴿رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ﴾: this nūn and wāw occur only in the plural of males among jinn and humans and the like. So one says: «الناس ساجدون» ("the people are prostrating"), and «الملائِكة والجِنّ ساجدون». If you go beyond this, the feminine and the masculine both pass to the feminine. So one says: «الكِباش قد ذُبَّحن» and «ذُبِّحت» and «مذبَّحات» ("the rams have been slaughtered"), and «مذبّحون» is not permissible. It was permitted with the sun, the moon and the stars with nūn and yāʾ only because they were described with the actions of human beings (do you not see that prostration and bowing come only from human beings? so their action was expressed in the form of the actions of human beings). Like it is ﴿وَقَالُوا لِجُلودِهِمْ لِمَ شَهِدْتُم عَلَيْنَا﴾: it is as though they addressed men, since they spoke to them and they spoke [back]. Likewise ﴿يَأَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ﴾. So whatever comes to you of non-humans performing the actions of human beings, treat it in this way.
[His saying] (يَا بُنىَّ) and (يا بُنىِّ) are two dialect forms, like your saying «يا أَبَتَ» and «يا أَبَتِ», because whoever uses fatḥa intends lamentation, «يا أبتاه», and has dropped it.
When the hamza of (الرُؤْيا) is left out, they say «الرُّويَا», seeking [to preserve the trace of] the hamza. And where it is their way to convert the hamza, they say «لا تقصص رُيّاك» in [ordinary] speech; but in the Qurʾān it is not permissible, because it would differ from the written text. Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited to me:
لعِرض من الأعراض يُمسى حَمَامُه * ويُضحى على أفنانِهِ العين يَهتِفُ
أحبّ إلى قلبى من الديك رُيَّة * وبابٍ إذا ما مال للغلق يَصرِف
(A valley among the valleys, whose doves coo at evening and in the morning on its branches, is dearer to my heart than the sight of a rooster and a door that creaks when it swings to be bolted.)
He meant «رُؤْية»; when he left out the hamza and a quiescent wāw came followed by a yāʾ, the two turned into a doubled yāʾ, as one says «لويته ليَّا» and «كويته كيّا», the original being «كَوْيا» and «لَوْيا». If you hint at the ḍamma and say «ريّا», with ḍamma on the rāʾ, it is permissible.
This ḍamma is like His saying (وحِيلَ) and (وسيق). al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard a Bedouin say: (إِن كُنْتُم للرِّيَّا تَعْبُرُون).

farraa:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ﴾ is an answer to His saying ﴿إنِّى رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً﴾: it was said to him: "And thus your Lord will choose you." «كذلك» and «هكذا» are the same in meaning. Its like in speech is that a man says: "Today I did such-and-such good and saw its outcome praiseworthy," and someone says to him: "Thus is felicity, thus is success" — and (كذلك) fits in it. (يَجْتَبِيكَ): He chooses you.

farraa:8-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ﴾: «العُصْبَة» is ten or more.
His saying: ﴿أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضاً يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ﴾ is an answer to the command, and the nominative is not sound in (يَخْلُ) because there is no pronoun in it [referring back]. Were you to say «أعِرْنى ثوباً ألبس» ("lend me a garment I [may] wear"), the nominative and the jussive would be permissible, because you mean «أَلْبَسُه» ("I wear it"); so it is nominative as part of the ṣila of the indefinite noun, and jussive if you make it a condition [i.e. apodosis].

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَلْقُوهُ فِي غَيَابَةِ ٱلْجُبِّ﴾: singular. The people of the Ḥijāz read (غَياَبَاتِ), in the plural. ﴿يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ ٱلسَّيَّارَةِ﴾: the general body of readers read it with yāʾ, because (بعض) is masculine even though it is annexed to a feminine. al-Ḥasan read — according to what is reported of him «[Note: MS B: «ذكروا» ("they reported")]» — (تَلْتَقِطْهُ) with tāʾ; that is because he referred it to «السيّارة». When the Arabs annex a masculine to a feminine, and it is an action of it or a part of it, they use both feminine and masculine in it. They recited to us:
على قبضة موجوءة ظهر كفّه * فلا المرء مُسْتحىٍ ولا هو طاعم
(On a handful [of food], the back of his hand struck — so the man is neither ashamed nor does he eat.)
He referred [the feminine] to «الكفّ» and disregarded «الظهر», because «الكف» suffices in place of «الظهر», so it is as though he said: «موجوءة كفُّه». al-ʿUklī Abū Tharwān recited to me:
أرى مَرَّ السنين أخذن منى * كما أخَذ السِّرار من الهلال
(I see that the passing of the years has taken from me, as the waning takes from the crescent.)
And Ibn Muqbil said:
قد صرَّح السير عن كُتْمان وابتُذلتْ * وَقْعُ المحاجن بالمَهْرِيَّة الذُقُنِ
(The journey has revealed [the camel] Kutmān, and the striking of the crooked sticks has been plied on the Mahrī camels that stretch their chins.)
He meant «وابتذلت المحاجن» and disregarded «الوقع». al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
إذا ماتَ منهم سَيّد قام سَيّد * فَدانَتْ له أهل القُرَى والكنائِسِ
(Whenever a lord of theirs dies, a lord arises, and the people of the towns and the churches submit to him.)
Of it also is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
وتَشرَقُ بالقول الذى قد أذعْتَه * كما شرِقت صدرُ القناة منَ الدَّم
(And you will choke on the words you have spread, as the upper shaft of the spear chokes with blood.)
And Yūnus al-Baṣrī recited to me:
لمّا أتى خبرُ الزُبَير تهدّمت * سورُ المدينة والجبالُ الخُشّعُ
(When the news of al-Zubayr came, the wall of the city crumbled, and the mountains humbled.)
All this was permitted only because the second suffices in place of the first; do you not see that had he said «تلتقطه السيَّارة», it would be permissible and would suffice in place of (بعض)? But it is not permissible to say «قد ضربْتنى غلامُ جاريتك» ("your slave-girl's boy has struck [fem.] me"), because if you dropped «الغلام», «الجارية» would not indicate its meaning.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ تَأْمَنَّا﴾: you hint at the ḍamma, and if you leave it, that is correct; each has been read. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read (تيمَنَّا).

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ﴾: whoever makes the ʿayn quiescent takes it from «القيد» and «الرَّتْعَة» (grazing freely), and it is then [of the pattern] «يفعل». Whoever says (يَرْتَعِ ويَلْعَبْ), it is «يفتعل» from «رعَيت» ("I pastured"), and he dropped the yāʾ for the jussive.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَآءُوا عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ﴾: its meaning is «مكذوب» ("lied about"). The Arabs say for «الكذب» "مكذوب" and for «الضعف» "مضعوف", and «ليس له عَقْد رأْى» and «معقودُ رأْىٍ» ("he has no firmness of judgement"); so in much of their speech they make the maṣdar (verbal noun) into a passive participle. They say: «هذا أمر ليس له مَعْنِىّ», meaning «مَعْنىً» ("meaning"), and they say for «الجَلَد» (endurance) «مجلود». The poet said:
* إن أخا المجلود من صَبَرَا *
(The man of endurance is the one who is patient.)
And another said:
حتّى إذا لم يتركوا لعظامه * لحماً ولا لفؤادهِ معقولاَ
(Until, when they had left no flesh on his bones nor any reason in his heart.)
And Abū Tharwān said: «إنّ بنى نُمَير ليس لحدّهم مكذوبة» ("the edge of the Banū Numayr has no falsity"). The meaning of His saying (بِدَمٍ كذِبٍ) is that they said to Jacob: "The wolf ate him," having dipped his shirt in the blood of a kid. He said: "This wolf was gentle with my son: it tore his skin and did not tear his clothes!" He said: And they said: "Robbers killed him." He said: "Then why did they leave his shirt?" — they being after clothes. That is why it was said (بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ). It is permissible in Arabic to say: «جاءوا على قميصه بدم كذباً», as you say: «جَاءوا بأمرٍ باطل» and «باطلا», «وحق» and «وحقاً».
His saying: ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾ is like His saying: ﴿فَصِيَامُ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ and ﴿فإِمْسَاكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾. Had it been «فَصَبَرا جميلاً», as one commanding himself to be patient, it would be permissible. In the reading of Ubayy it is (فَصَبْرا جَمِيلاً), likewise in the accusative with alif.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰبُشْرَىٰ هَـٰذَا غُلاَمٌ﴾ — (وَيَا بشراىَ) with fatḥa on the yāʾ, which is a dialect form among some of Qays. Hudhayl [say]: «يا بُشْرَىَّ»: every alif that the speaker annexes to himself they make into a doubled yāʾ. al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn recited to me:
تركوا هوَىّ وأعْنَقوا لهواهم * ففقدتهم ولكل جَنْب مَصْرع
(They abandoned my desire and hastened to their own desire, so I lost them; and every side has its place of falling.)
One of the Banū Sulaym said to me: «آتيك بمولَيَّ فإنه أروى منّى» ("I will bring you my patron, for he knows more [poetry] by heart than I"). He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
يطوِّف بى عِكَبّ فى مَعَدّ * ويطعُن بالصُمُلَّة فى قَفَيَّا
فإن لم تَثْأَروا لى من عِكَبّ * فلا أرويتما أبداً صَدَيَّا
(ʿIkabb parades me around among Maʿadd and jabs the stick into the back of my neck; if you do not avenge me on ʿIkabb, may you never quench my thirst.)
Whoever reads (يا بُشْرَىْ) with sukūn, it is like your saying «يا بُنْى لا تفعل» ("my son, do not!"): it is singular with the meaning of annexation. The Arabs say «يا نفسُ اصبرى» and «يا نفسِ اصبرى» ("O soul, be patient"), meaning himself in both ways. And (يا بُشْرَاىَ) is in the position of the accusative. Whoever says «يا بشرَىَّ», annexing and changing the alif to yāʾ, sought the kasra that always attaches to what precedes the speaker's yāʾ in every case; do you not see that you say «هذا غلامِى», giving the mīm kasra in all cases of i'rab? So they lowered it [to kasra] when annexed to the speaker, and did not lower it with other than the yāʾ, as in your saying «هذا غلامك» and «غلامه»; because (يا بُشْرَى) is from «البشارة», and i'rab is apparent with every pronoun except the yāʾ. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «ألا أنك تقول ... فتحفض», evidently for «ألا ترى أنك تقول ... فتخفض».]»
His saying: ﴿وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَاعَةً﴾: that is because the water-drawer who picked him up said to those who were with him: "If your companions ask you about this boy, say: The people of the water gave him to us as merchandise to sell for them in Egypt."

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ دَرَاهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ﴾: it was said: twenty. It was said «معدودة» ("counted") only to indicate their fewness, because they did not weigh dirhams until they reached an ūqiyya, which was the weight of forty dirhams.
His saying: ﴿وَكَانُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّاهِدِينَ﴾. He is saying: they did not know his rank with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ﴾: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and his companions read it [so]. al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā related to me from Abū Ḥabīb, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to read (هَيْتَ). It is said that it is a dialect of the people of Ḥawrān that came to Mecca, and they spoke it. The people of Medina read «هِيتَ لك» with kasra on the hāʾ and without hamza. It is reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Ibn ʿAbbās that they read (هِئتُ لك), meaning by it: "I have made myself ready for you." The poet said:
أنّ العِراق وَأَهْلَه * سَلْمٌ عَلَيْكَ فَهَيتَ هَيْتَا
(Iraq and its people are at peace with you, so come, come!)
that is, «هَلُمَّ» ("come").
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ رَبِّيۤ﴾ means his master who bought him. He is saying: he has treated me well, so I will not betray him.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿أَن رَّأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ﴾: they reported that he saw the image of Jacob (peace be upon him).

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَى ٱلْبَابِ﴾ means Joseph and the wife of al-ʿAzīz found al-ʿAzīz and a cousin of his wife at the door. She said: ﴿مَا جَزَآءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوۤءًا﴾, and he said: ﴿هى راودتنى عن [نفسى]﴾. They reported that her cousin said: ﴿إِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ قُبُلٍ فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ وَإِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾. When they saw the shirt torn from behind, the cousin said: ﴿إِنَّهُ مِنْ كَيْدِكُنَّ إِنَّ كَيْدَكُنَّ عَظِيمٌ﴾. Then the cousin made a request of Joseph and said: ﴿أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذَا﴾, that is, conceal it; and he said to the other: (استَغْفِرِى) your husband (لِذَنْبِكِ).

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ﴾. He said: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ related to me from Abū Ḥaṣīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying: ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ﴾; he said: a child. He said: And Qays related to me from a man, from Mujāhid, that he was a man. He said: And Muʿallā ibn Hilāl related to me from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying ﴿وَشهد شاهد من أهلها﴾; he said: a judge from her family judged.
Had there been in the speech (أَنْ إِنْ كان قميصُه), it would be sound, because testimony is followed by (أن) and does not make do with the conditional [alone]. When it does make do [with it], the testimony is taken in the sense of "saying," as though He said: "and a speaker from her family said," just as He said: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللهُ فىِ أَوْلاَدِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾, taking the bequest in the sense of saying. al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
وخَبَّرتُما أَنْ إِنَّمَا بَينِ بِيشَةٍ * ونَجْران أَحْوَى والمحَلّ قَرٍيبُ
(You two told me that between Bīsha and Najrān [the land] is dark green, and the camping place is near)
(and the area fertile). So he brought «أن» in on «إنما», and it is in the same position. He said: And I heard al-Farrāʾ say: al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn claimed that «بِئشة» and «زِئنة» are two lands with hamza.

farraa:30-31.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبّاً﴾, that is, it has pierced the pericardium (shaghāf) of her heart. It is also read (قَدْ شَعَفَهَا) with ʿayn, which is from your saying «شُعِف بها» ("he was infatuated with her"), as though it carried her off in every direction. «الشَعَف» is the tops of the mountains.
His saying: ﴿وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَئاً﴾: it is said: she prepared a sitting place for them. And it is said that it is «مُتْكاً», without hamza, and I heard that it is the citron. And a shaykh among the trustworthy people of Basra told me that he said: it is al-zumāward (a dish of meat rolled in bread).
His saying: ﴿وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ﴾. He is saying: they scratched them, without severing their hands, out of their awe of him; and that is His saying: ﴿حَاشَ للَّهِ﴾: they held him too great to be a human being, and said: "This is an angel." In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (حَاشَا لِلّه) with alif, and it has the sense of «مَعَاذ الله» ("Allah forbid").
His saying: ﴿مَا هَـٰذَا بَشَراً﴾: you put (بَشراً) in the accusative because the bāʾ is used in it, and the people of the Ḥijāz hardly ever pronounce it except with the bāʾ; when they dropped it, they wanted it to leave a trace on what it had left, so they used the accusative on that basis. Do you not see that everything in the Qurʾān comes with the bāʾ except this and His saying: ﴿مَا هُنَّ أُمّهَاتِهِمْ﴾? As for the people of Najd, they speak with the bāʾ and without the bāʾ, and when they drop it they use the nominative; and that is the stronger of the two ways in Arabic. Someone recited to me:
لَشتَّان ما أنوِى وينوِى بنو أبى * جَميعاً فما هذان مستويان
تَمنَّوا لىَ الموتَ الذى يَشْعَب الفتى * وكلُّ فتىً والموتُ يلتقيانِ
(How different is what I intend and what my father's sons all intend — these two are not equal! They wished for me the death that parts a young man [from his people]; and every young man and death will meet.)
And they recited to me:
ركابُ حُسَيل أَشهرَ الصيف بُدْن * وناقةُ عَمْرو ما يُحَلُّ لها رَحلُ
ويزعم حِسْلٌ أَنه فَرْع قومِهِ * وما أَنت فرع يا حُسيل ولا أصْلُ
(Ḥusayl's riding camels are fat in the summer months, while ʿAmr's she-camel never has her saddle taken off; and Ḥisl claims he is the top branch of his people — but you are neither branch nor root, O Ḥusayl.)
And al-Farazdaq said:
أَمَا نحن راءُو دارِها بعد هذه * يدَ الدهر إلا أنَّ يمرّ بها سَفْرُ
(We shall not see her abode after this, for all time, unless travellers pass by it.)
If you put the "verb" (the predicate adjective) before the noun, you put the predicate and its noun in the nominative and say: «ما سامعٌ هذا» and «ما قائم أخوك» ("your brother is not standing"). That is because the bāʾ is not used here and does not enter; do you not see that it is ugly to say «ما بقائم أخوك», because it occurs in the negated [predicate] only when the noun comes first? Since (ما) cannot contain a pronoun of the noun, the entry of the bāʾ is ugly. But that is good with (ليس): to say «ليس بقائم أخوك», because (ليس) is a verb that accepts a pronoun, as in your saying «لست» and «لسنا»; and that is not possible with (ما).
If you say: "I see that this is not possible with (لا) either, yet the Arabs brought the bāʾ into the predicate that follows it, saying:
* لا بالْحَصُور ولا فِيها بسوَّارِ *
(neither stingy nor quarrelsome over it)"
I say: (لا) resembles «ليس» more than (ما) does; do you not see that you say «عبدالله لا قائم ولا قاعد» ("ʿAbd Allāh is neither standing nor sitting"), as you say «عبدالله ليس قاعداً ولا قائماً», but «عبدالله ما قائم ولا قاعد» is not permissible? So the two differ here.
Were you to carry the bāʾ over to (ما) when the predicate follows it, imagining in it what you imagined in (لا), it would be a valid way. A woman of Ghanī recited to me:
أَما واللهِ أن لو كنتَ حُرّاً * وما بالْحُرّ أنتَ ولا العَتِيقِ
(By Allah, if you were a free man — but you are not a free man, nor a freed one.)
She brought the bāʾ into what follows (مَا). If you drop it, you use the nominative, and the accusative is not strong because this is rare. He said: And al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Diʿāma ibn Rajāʾ al-Taymī — and he was naive — related to me from Abū al-Ḥuwayrith al-Ḥanafī that he said: (ما هذا بِشِرًى), that is, "this is not one to be bought."

farraa:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿رَبِّ ٱلسِّجْنُ﴾: «السِّجن» is the place of confinement, and it is like the verb [i.e. the verbal noun]. Every noun of place derived from a verb stands in the place of the verb, as the Arabs say: «طلعت الشمسُ مَطْلِعاً» and «غَرَبت الشمس مغرِباً» ("the sun rose a rising, set a setting"): they made them substitutes for the maṣdar (verbal noun), though they are both nouns [of place]. Likewise «السِّجن». Had you given the sīn fatḥa, it would be a clear maṣdar; and it has been read (رَبِّ السَّجْنُ).

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾, though there was no request from him; he only said: ﴿إِلاَّ تَصْرِفْ عَنِّى كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ﴾, and Allah made it a supplication because it has the meaning of supplication; that is why He said: ﴿فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾. Its like in speech is that you say to your slave: "If you do not obey, you will be punished," and he says: "Then I will obey you" — as though you had said to him "Obey!" and he answered you.

farraa:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُاْ ٱلآيَاتِ﴾: the signs of innocence, the tearing of the shirt from behind. ﴿لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ﴾: this lām occurs in oaths and in everything resembling "saying," and we have mentioned it. Do you not see His saying: ﴿وَظَنُّوا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ﴾ and ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمن اشْتَرَاهُ﴾? This lām and (ما) entered with "thinking" (and "knowing") because they have the meaning of saying and of an oath.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾. He is saying: of the knowledgeable; you have mastered knowledge well. al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Ibn al-Ghasīl al-Anṣārī related to us from ʿIkrima, who said: «الحين» is of two kinds: a ḥīn that cannot be determined, which is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هَلْ أَتَى عَلَى الإنْسَانِ حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ﴾ (al-Farrāʾ said: this may be short or long); it has no limit. ʿIkrima said: and a ḥīn that can be determined, which is His saying: ﴿تُؤْتِى أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍ﴾, meaning six months.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ﴾. He is saying: of its cause and its kinds. His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ بِٱلآخِرَةِ هُمْ كَافِرُونَ﴾: the Arabs do not combine two pronouns (kināya) with nothing between them unless they intend repetition and making the person addressed understand; when they want that, they say: «أنت أنت فعلت» ("you — you did [it]") and «هو هو أخذها» ("he — he took it"). And we may not make the second an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first, because their wording is identical. But when they join the first [pronoun] to something that governs it in the accusative, genitive or nominative, they bring in its [independent] noun for it, and it is then emphasis. As for the accusative: your saying «ضربتك أنت» ("I struck you, you"); the genitive: «مررت بك أَنت»; the nominative: «قمتَ أَنت». They did that only because the first was short and different in wording, so they brought in its independent (mubtadaʾ) pronoun. When they say «أَنت فينا أنت رَاغب» ("you, among us, you are desirous"), separating the two by an adverbial phrase (ṣifa), they say it; and in its manner it is like His saying: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَنْ تَوَلاَّهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ﴾, as though the first were void and the reliance and the predicate were on the second. Likewise His saying: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إذَا مِتُّمْ﴾, then He said: ﴿أَنَّكُمْ مخْرَجُون﴾, and both have one meaning; but that was permitted when they were separated by «إذا». Like it is: ﴿وَهُمْ بِالآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ﴾.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ آبَآئِـيۤ﴾: you pronounce the hamza and retain the yāʾ in it. Our companions transmit from al-Aʿmash ﴿مِلَّةَ آبَاىَ إبراهيمَ﴾ and ﴿دُعَاىَ إِلاَّ فِرَاراً﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ, because he drops the hamza and shortens the long [alif], so it becomes like «مَحْياىَ» and «هداىَ».

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿قُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ﴾: they reported that when he interpreted the dream for them and said to the other: "You will be crucified," the two retracted the dream and said: "We saw nothing." So Joseph said: ﴿قُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ﴾.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَنْسَاهُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ﴾.
He is saying: Satan made Joseph forget to make his remembrance and his call for help to Allah. And it is said: Satan made the cupbearer forget to mention Joseph's affair.
His saying: ﴿ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ﴾. He is saying: Joseph's mention [of him] to his master.
His saying: ﴿فَلَبِثَ فِي ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ﴾: they reported that he remained seven [years] after five; and «البِضع» is less than ten.

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ﴾. It is of the speech of the Arabs that a man says: "I see [myself] going out to Mecca," and other such things, and it is known that it refers to sleep. Had he meant a report, he would have said: "I am doing," "I am standing." So it is inferred that it is a dream from his saying «أَرى» ("I see"), even though he does not mention sleep. Abraham (peace be upon him) made it explicit and said: ﴿إنّى أَرَى فىِ المَنَام أَنِّى أَذْبَحُكَ﴾.

farraa:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلاَمٍ﴾ is nominative, because they meant: "This is nothing; it is only [a matter of] jumbled dreams." It is like His saying: ﴿مَاذَا أَنْزلَ رَبَّكُمْ قالوا أَسَا طِيرُ الأَوَّلِينَ﴾: they disbelieved and said: "He has sent down nothing; it is only the tales of the ancients." Had it been (أَضغاثَ أَحلاَمٍ) [in the accusative], that is, "you have seen jumbled dreams," it would be correct.

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ﴾: «الأمة» is a period of time. It is reported of one of them that [he read] (بَعْدَ أَمَهٍ), which is forgetfulness. One says «رجل مأموه», as though he were the one whose reason is not with him; and «قد أمِهَ الرجُل» ("the man has forgotten").

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿وَسَبْعِ سُنبُلاَتٍ خُضْرٍ﴾: had «الخضر» been accusative, made a naʿt (adjective) of «السّبْع», that would be good; when it is genitive it is an adjective of «السنبلات». And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَوَاتٍ طِبَاقاً﴾; had it been (طباقٍ), it would be correct.

farraa:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿دَأَباً﴾: some of our readers read (سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَباً) [on the pattern] «فَعَلاً». Likewise every word whose first letter has fatḥa and whose second is quiescent may be given a vowel on the second when that second is a hamza, ʿayn, ghayn, ḥāʾ, khāʾ or hāʾ.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ﴾. He is saying: what you have set aside in advance for them of the crops.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلآنَ حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾: when he summoned the women and they declared him innocent, she said [to herself]: nothing remains but that he will turn to me to make me confess; so she confessed. That is His saying: ﴿حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾. He is saying: the lie has been hemmed in and the truth has become clear.

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِٱلْغَيْبِ﴾: Joseph said that when the cupbearer returned to him and told him of the women's declaring him innocent. So Joseph said ﴿ذٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِٱلْغَيْبِ﴾, and it is joined to the saying of his [master's] wife: ﴿اْلآنَ حَصْحَصَ الحَقُّ أَنَا رَاوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ ذَلِكَ﴾. Sometimes speech is joined to speech until it seems to be the saying of one person, while it is the speech of two; this is of that kind. And His saying ﴿مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِ فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾: Pharaoh's saying is joined to the saying of the chiefs. Likewise His saying ﴿إنَّ المُلُوكَ إذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا﴾ up to His saying ﴿وكَذَلكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾: her speech ended at His saying ﴿أَذِلَّةً﴾, then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾. And it is said that it is the saying of Solomon (peace be upon him). «[Translator's note: the source says «امرأته» ("his wife"), referring to the wife of al-ʿAzīz.]»

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لأَمَّارَةٌ بِٱلسُّوۤءِ إِلاَّ مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّيۤ﴾: (ما) is in the position of the accusative. It is an exception cut off (munqaṭiʿ) from what precedes. Like it is ﴿إلاَّ حَاجَةً فىِ نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا﴾, and like it in Sūrat Yā Sīn: ﴿فلا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يُنْقَذُونَ إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا﴾: it is only — and Allah knows best — "except that they be shown mercy." And (أن) resembles (ما) when both have the meaning of a maṣdar.

farraa:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْرَبُونِ﴾ is in the position of the jussive, and the nūn is in the position of the accusative, its yāʾ having been dropped. Had you made it nominative and given the nūn fatḥa, it would be correct, in the sense of "and you will not come near after this," like His saying ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ﴾ and ﴿الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشَاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾.

farraa:62-62.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَانِهِ﴾ and (لِفِتْيَتِهِ) are two widespread readings.
His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنْقَلَبُوۤاْ﴾: two views have been stated about it. One of them is that Joseph feared that his father would have no dirhams, so he put the merchandise in their saddlebags so that they would return. And it was said: if they recognised that it was their merchandise after they had received their measure, they would return it to Joseph and not consider it lawful to keep it.

farraa:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَآ أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ﴾: the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read (يَكْتَلْ), and the rest of the people (نَكْتَلْ). Both are correct. Whoever says (نَكْتَلْ) includes him with them in the measure; whoever says (يكْتَلْ) [means] he receives a measure for himself, making the verb his alone, because by him they would be given an extra camel-load.

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَافِظاً﴾, and «حِفْظاً». In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (والله خير الحافظين), and this is evidence for both ways together. That is because when you annex «أفضل» (the elative) to something, it is part of it; and dropping the genitive noun is permissible while you intend it. If you wish, you make it «خيرهم حفظاً» ("the best of them in guarding"), dropping the hāʾ and mīm while they are intended in the meaning; and if you wish, you make (حافظا) a specification (tafsīr) of the elative. It is like your saying: «لك أفضلهم رجلاً» ("you have the best of them as a man"), then you drop the hāʾ and mīm and say: «لك أفضل رَجُلاً» and «خير رجُلاً». The Arabs say: «لك أفضلها كَبْشا» ("you have the best of them as a ram"), and it is only a specification of the elative.
al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Abū Laylā al-Sijistānī related to us from Abū Ḥarīz, the judge of Sijistān, that Ibn Masʿūd read (فالله خير حافظا); and I have informed you that it is written in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh (خَيْرُ الحَافِظِينَ). This man — meaning Abū Laylā — was known for goodness. And he related to us with this chain from ʿAbd Allāh that he read ﴿فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَوْقعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ and ﴿وإنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ﴾ — they say [it means] "equipped with weapons," from «آدى يُؤدِى».

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿يٰأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي﴾ is like your saying in speech: "What do you want?" Then He said ﴿هَـٰذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا﴾, as though they were reassuring him. (مَا) is an interrogative in the position of the accusative. Its meaning may also be negation, as though they said: "We do not want dirhams from you." And Allah knows best what is correct in that.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ﴾. He is saying: unless something comes upon you from Allah that excuses you.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿يٰبَنِيَّ لاَ تَدْخُلُواْ مِن بَابٍ وَاحِدٍ﴾. He is saying: do not enter Egypt by one road. They were handsome, and the [evil] eye would strike them.

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِّمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ﴾. He is saying: he is possessed of knowledge because of Our teaching him. And it is said: he is retentive of what We taught him.

farraa:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَبْتَئِسْ﴾: its meaning is: do not be abased by grief and misery. He is saying: do not grieve.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ﴾ is an answer [to «لمّا»]. Sometimes the Arabs bring the wāw into the like of it while it remains an answer, as in His saying at the beginning of the sūra ﴿فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا بِهِ وَأَجْمَعْوا أَنْ يَجْعَلُوهُ فىِ غَيَابَةِ الْجُبِّ وَأَوْحَيْنَا إلَيْهِ﴾, the meaning being — and Allah knows best —: "We revealed to him." In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (فَلَمَا جَهَّزهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ وَجَعَلَ السِّقَايَةَ). Its like in speech: «لمَّا أتانى وأثِبَ عليه», as though he said: "I leapt on him." Sometimes the Arabs bring «لكن» into the answer of «لَمَّا», and a man says: «لَمَّا شتَمنى لكن أَثِبُ عَليه» ("when he insulted me — but I leap on him"), as though he began the speech afresh, imagining that what preceded contained its answer. (Poetry has come with all of that.) Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فلمَّا أَجَزْنا ساحة الحَىّ وانتحى * بنا بطنُ خَبْت ذى قِفافٍ عَقَنْقَلِ
(And when we had crossed the tribe's open ground, and the hollow of a plain with hillocks and winding sand-dunes took us aside.)
And another said:
حتَّي إِذا قمِلت بطونُكم * ورأيتُم أبْناءكم شَبُّوا
وقلبتم ظهر المِجَنِّ لنَا * إنّ اللّئيم العاجزُ الْخَبُّ
(Until, when your bellies grew fat, and you saw your sons grown up, and you turned the back of the shield against us — truly the base man is the feeble deceiver.)
«قمِلت»: grew fat and large.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ ٱلْمَلِكِ﴾. «الصُّواع» is masculine; it is the vessel from which the king used to drink. «الصاع» is feminine and masculine. Whoever makes it feminine says «ثلاث أصْوُع», like «ثلاث أَدْؤُر»; and whoever makes it masculine says «ثلاثة أصواع», like «أبواب». His saying ﴿وَأَنَاْ بِهِ زَعِيمٌ﴾. He is saying: guarantor. And the «زعيم» of a people is their chief.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿تَٱللَّهِ﴾: the Arabs do not say «تالرحمنِ», and they do not put tāʾ in place of the wāw except with "Allah," Mighty and Majestic. That is because it is the most current of oaths in speech, so they imagined that the wāw was part of it because of its frequency in speech, and replaced it with tāʾ, as they said «التُّرَاث» ("inheritance"), which is from «ورث», and as He said ﴿رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَى﴾, which is from «المواترة», and as they said «التُخَمة» ("indigestion"), which is from «الوَخَامة», and «التُّجاه» ("direction"), which is from «واجهك».
His saying ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَّا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ﴾. Someone may ask: how did they know that they had not come to make mischief or to steal? It is reported that on their way they did not stop with anyone unjustly, and did not stop in people's orchards and damage them. That is His saying ﴿مَّا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ﴾. He is saying: had we been thieves, we would not have returned to you the merchandise that we found in our saddlebags.

farraa:75-75.t: His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ جَزَآؤُهُ مَن وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ﴾: (من) has the meaning of a conditional (jazāʾ), and its position is nominative by the hāʾ that refers back. The answer of the conditional is the fāʾ in His saying: (فَهُوَ جَزَاؤهُ). And the second (جزاؤه) is nominative by the meaning carried in the conditional and its answer. Its like in speech is that you say: «ماذا لى عندك؟» ("what do I have from you?"), and he says: «لك عندى إن بشّرتنى فلك أَلف درهم» ("you have from me: if you bring me good news, you shall have a thousand dirhams"), as though he said: "you have this from me." If you wish, you may take (مَن) in the manner of (الذى), and the fāʾ enters the predicate of (مَن) when it has the meaning of (الذى), as you say: «الذى يقوم فإنَّا نَقوم معه» ("whoever stands, we will stand with him"). And if you wish, you may make «الجزاء» nominative by «مَنْ» alone with its ṣila, as though you said: "its recompense is the one found in his saddlebag," as though you said: "his reward is to be enslaved"; then you also begin afresh and say: "that is its recompense." It was their custom to enslave whoever stole. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «ماذالى» and «يترقّوا», evidently for «ماذا لى» and «يسترقّوا».]»

farraa:76-76.t:
Then He said: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَخْرَجَهَا﴾: He referred it to the feminine «السَّرقة» (the stolen thing). If «الصُّوَاع» has the meaning of «الصَّاع», then perhaps this feminine is from that. And if you wish, you may make it for the feminine of «السِّقاية».
His saying ﴿نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ﴾: (مَنْ) is in the position of the accusative, that is: "We raise whom We will by degrees."
He is saying: We prefer whom We will by degrees. Whoever says (نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتِ مَنْ نشَاءُ), (مَن) is then in the position of the genitive.
His saying ﴿وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾. He is saying: there is no learned man but that above him is one more learned than he.

farraa:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِي نَفْسِهِ﴾: he kept the word secret. Had He said (فأسرَّه), referring to the masculine «الكلام», it would be correct, as in His saying ﴿تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الغَيْبِ﴾ and ﴿ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الغَيْبِ﴾. ﴿وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا لَهُمْ﴾: he concealed it within himself and did not reveal it.

farraa:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is accusative because it is a maṣdar; and every maṣdar whose meaning the Arabs express with «فَعَل» or «يفعل», the accusative is permissible in it. Of that is «الحمدَ لله», because you may say in its place «يحمد الله». Likewise «أعوذ بالله» fits in the meaning of «معاذَ الله».

farraa:80-80.t:
His saying: ﴿خَلَصُواْ نَجِيّاً﴾, and [«نَجوَى»]; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿مَا يَكُون مِن نَجْوَى ثَلاَثَةٍ﴾. His saying: ﴿قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَّوْثِقاً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمْ﴾: the (ما) with (فَرَّطْتُمْ) is in the position of the nominative, as though he said: "and before this [was] your failing regarding Joseph."
If you wish, you may make it accusative, that is: "Do you not know this, and know your earlier failing regarding Joseph?" And if you wish, you may make (ما) a ṣila (redundant), as though he said: ﴿ومن قبلُ فرَّطتم فى يوسف﴾.

farraa:81-81.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱبْنَكَ سَرَقَ﴾. It is also read (سُرِّق) ("was accused of theft"), but I do not favour it, because it is anomalous (shādhdh). It is as though [its reader] took the view that he would not consider it lawful [to say he stole] when he was [only] accused of theft and had not stolen. It is reported that Maymūn ibn Mihrān met Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa in Mecca. Rajāʾ used to say: lying is not right, in earnest or in jest; and Maymūn used to say: many a lie is better than much truth. He said: Maymūn said to Rajāʾ: "Who was your travelling companion?" He said: "A man of Qays." He said: "Suppose that, when you passed by al-Bishr, Taghlib had said to you: 'You are the utmost in truthfulness, so who is this companion of yours? If he is of Qays, we will kill him — and you know how many of us Qays have killed' — would you have said 'of Qays' or 'of other than Qays'?" He said: "Rather, of other than Qays." He said: "So was that [lie] better, or the truth?" al-Farrāʾ said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has granted the prophets stratagems greater than this. And Allah knows best the interpretation of that. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «فأن كان مِنْ قيس قتلناة», evidently for «فإن كان من قيس قتلناه».]»
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا لِلْغَيْبِ حَافِظِينَ﴾. He is saying: we were not guarding your son's unseen [affairs], nor do we know what he does when he is absent from us. And it is said: had we known that this would happen, we would not have taken him out with us.

farraa:83-83.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْراً فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾: «الصبر الجميل» is nominative because he was consoling himself and said: "It is nothing but patience." Had he commanded them to be patient, the accusative would be easier, as the poet said:
يَشْكو إِلىَّ جملى طول السُّرى * صَبراً جميلاً فكلانا مُبْتَلَى
(My camel complains to me of the long night-journey: beautiful patience! for both of us are afflicted.)
His saying: ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾. He is saying: there is no complaint in it except to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

farraa:85-85.t:
They said: ﴿تَالله تَفْتَؤُاْ﴾: its meaning is "you will not cease remembering Joseph." (لا) may be implied with oaths, because when [the oath's complement] is an affirmative statement in which (لا) is not implied, it must be with a lām; do you not see that you say «والله لآتينَّكَ» ("by Allah, I will surely come to you"), and it is not permissible to say «والله آتيك» unless you intend (لا)? Since its position is clear, having parted from the affirmative statement, it is implied. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فقلت يَمينَ الله أبرح قاعداً * ولو قطعوا رأسى لديكِ وأوصَالى
(I said: By Allah's oath, I will not cease sitting [here], even if they cut off my head and my limbs beside you.)
Someone recited to me:
فلا وأبى دَهْمَاء زالت عزيزةً * عَلَى قَوْمها ما فَتَّل الزَّنْدَ قادح
(No — by Dahmāʾ's father! — she will not cease to be dear to her people, as long as a fire-maker twirls the fire-stick.)
He means «لا زالت». His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضاً﴾: one says «رجل حَرَض», «امرأة حَرَض» and «قوم حَرَض»; it is singular in every case: masculine, feminine and plural are the same in it. Some Arabs say «حارِض» for the masculine and «حارضة» for the feminine, and make the dual and plural here, because it has come out in the form of «فاعل», and «فاعل» is pluralised. «الحارض» is one corrupted in body or mind. It is said of a man: «إنه لحارض», that is, foolish; and [it also means] one corrupted in his mind. As for «حَرَض», its plural was not used because it is a maṣdar, like «دَنَف» and «ضَنىً» (wasting illness). The Arabs say: «قوم دنَف», «ضَنىً», «عدْل», «رِضا», «زَوْر», «عَوْد» and «ضَيْف». Had it been put in the dual and plural, it would be correct, as they said «ضيف» and «أضياف». He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿أنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَينِ مِثْلِنَا﴾, and He said in another place: ﴿مَا أَنْتُمْ إلاَّ بَشَرٌ﴾. The Arabs are quicker to the dual than to its plural, because the singular may have the meaning of a plural but does not have the meaning of two; do you not see that you say «كم عندك من درهم» and «من دراهم» ("how many dirhams do you have?"), but «كم عندك من درهمين» is not permissible? That is why the dual became frequent and the plural was not used.
